*High Artificer Gardesano's account, as transcribed by Amanuensis Nofra*  

I have made a breakthrough with my newest pupils. Some of my fellow docents at the main conservatoire here in Stellis Quor's Luminous Ward had their misgivings, but what good is the experience of a proper education without space to pursue one's fancies, one's passions? The mursaat we admit to study in Stellis Quor should come to know Tyria as we do—its power, its beauty, and its dangers, within reason. But I digress; last week's lessons were something of a personal interest to me.  

In recent days, both Elka and Antenor have taken a growing interest in my stewards, and so I offered to instruct them in the delicate craft of shaping and enchanting their own constructs. Even with these rudimentary lessons and my limited facilities in the city, Elka was able to follow my methods to the letter as if she were my very shadow. And she produced an impressive first attempt, a near perfect simulacrum of one of my own stewards with some noticeable differences in flair.  

Antenor... He took an unorthodox approach, asking if he could supply his own materials and returning the following day with several large purple jadestones; an inspired choice, I thought. Jade has shown potential in the use of arcane constructs. But, for reasons I've yet to discern, it's a material that takes greater arcane input to reach a functional baseline than other materials I've experimented with, and I prefer to lean toward efficiency. Nonetheless, Antenor was both diligent and insouciant; it took him much longer than Elka to finish his first construct, but it paid off. The bulky thing was even able to hover with the best of us.  

I still smile when I think about their work and the potential their newfound crafts could provide for them and their people. It will be an honor to watch and see what becomes of their studies. Such is the unique pride of a teacher.
